raw_text:
# 12-Week General Fitness Programme: Post-MI Client (Male, 58)

## Before You Start

- **Get written parameters from cardiac rehab.** Confirm the HR ceiling, any BP limits, medication (especially beta-blockers, which blunt heart rate and make HR zones unreliable), and whether they want ECG monitoring or a symptom log.
- **Use RPE as the primary intensity guide.** Target **RPE 11–13 (Borg 6–20)** or a "can talk in full sentences" effort. Use HR as a secondary check, and cap it at 115 bpm or whatever rehab specifies.
- **Stop and refer** if he reports chest pain or pressure, unusual breathlessness, dizziness, palpitations, nausea, pain radiating to the arm, jaw, or back, or unusual fatigue. Do not train through these symptoms.
- **Monitor BP** before and after sessions in the early weeks if rehab requests it. Stop if resting systolic is above roughly 160 or diastolic above 100, per most rehab protocols, and confirm local thresholds.

## Session Guardrails (All Phases)

- **Breathing:** Exhale on exertion, never hold breath. No Valsalva.
- **Loading:** Work at about 50–65% of estimated 1RM, or choose a load where the last 2–3 reps feel like RPE 6–7 out of 10. Never train to failure.
- **Rest:** 90–120 seconds between sets, so HR can recover.
- **Avoid:** Maximal or near-maximal lifts, heavy overhead pressing in early weeks, heavy isometric holds, sprinting, high-intensity intervals, and heavy bracing or straining movements such as heavy deadlifts or max-effort carries.
- **Warm-up (5–10 min):** Walk or cycle at low effort, then dynamic mobility.
- **Cool-down (5–10 min):** Gradual reduction in effort, then light stretching and breathing.

## Weekly Structure

- **3 strength sessions** (non-consecutive days, e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri)
- **2 aerobic sessions** (e.g., Tue/Sat), 20–40 minutes at RPE 11–13
- **1 rest or active recovery day** (Sun)

---

## Phase 1: Weeks 1–4, Foundation and Adaptation

**Goal:** Establish movement quality, build tolerance, and learn his RPE. Keep effort very conservative.

**Aerobic:** 15–20 minutes at RPE 10–11, increasing by 2–3 minutes per week. Treadmill walking, recumbent bike, or elliptical.

**Strength (Full-Body A/B alternating):**

*Session A*
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Leg press | 2 × 12 | Light load, controlled tempo |
| Seated chest press machine | 2 × 12 | Exhale on press |
| Seated row machine | 2 × 12 | Keep shoulders relaxed |
| Lat pulldown | 2 × 12 | Light-moderate load |
| Seated leg curl | 2 × 12 | |
| Dead bug or bird dog | 2 × 8/side | Core stability, breathe throughout |

*Session B*
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Goblet squat (to box) | 2 × 10 | Light dumbbell, exhale on standing |
| Dumbbell floor press | 2 × 12 | |
| Cable seated row | 2 × 12 | |
| Leg extension | 2 × 12 | |
| Glute bridge | 2 × 12 | |
| Standing calf raise | 2 × 15 | Support on a rail |

**Progression:** Week 1 establishes baseline and RPE. Weeks 2–4 add a rep or small load only if sessions feel RPE 6 or lower and he reports no symptoms. Do not add sets yet.

---

## Phase 2: Weeks 5–8, Build

**Goal:** Increase work capacity and muscular strength at moderate loads.

**Aerobic:** 25–30 minutes at RPE 11–13. Add interval-style variation only if cleared: 2 minutes at RPE 12–13 alternating with 3 minutes at RPE 10–11. Keep HR under the ceiling throughout.

**Strength (Full-Body A/B):**

*Session A*
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Leg press | 3 × 10–12 | Increase load gradually |
| Machine chest press | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Seated cable row | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Lat pulldown | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Romanian deadlift (light, dumbbells) | 3 × 10 | Hip hinge, neutral spine, no straining |
| Plank (short holds) | 3 × 15–20 sec | Breathe; stop before form breaks |

*Session B*
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Goblet squat | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Incline dumbbell press (30°) | 3 × 10–12 | Avoid steep incline |
| Single-arm dumbbell row | 3 × 10–12/side | |
| Seated leg curl | 3 × 10–12 | |
| Step-ups (low box) | 3 × 8/side | Support available |
| Cable face pull | 3 × 12–15 | Light, shoulder health |

**Progression:** Add load when all sets feel RPE 6–7 or lower. Keep reps in the 10–12 range. Introduce supported single-leg work only if balance is good.

---

## Phase 3: Weeks 9–12, Consolidate and Expand

**Goal:** Build general strength, endurance, and confidence. Consolidate habits he can sustain long-term.

**Aerobic:** 30–40 minutes at RPE 11–13, mixing modalities (bike, walk, rower at easy pace). Optional: add a longer weekly session of 40–45 minutes if he's comfortable.

**Strength (Full-Body A/B/C rotation, 3 sessions/week):**

*Session A (Lower emphasis)*
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Leg press | 3 × 10–12 |
| Seated leg curl | 3 × 10–12 |
| Walking lunges (light DBs, supported) | 2 × 8/side |
| Standing calf raise | 3 × 12–15 |
| Pallof press | 2 × 10/side |

*Session B (Upper emphasis)*
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Machine or flat DB chest press | 3 × 10–12 |
| Seated cable row | 3 × 10–12 |
| Lat pulldown | 3 × 10–12 |
| Lateral raise (light) | 2 × 12–15 |
| Band or cable triceps pushdown | 2 × 12 |

*Session C (Full body)*
| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|
| Goblet squat | 3 × 10–12 |
| Dumbbell Romanian deadlift | 3 × 10 |
| Incline dumbbell press | 3 × 10–12 |
| Cable row | 3 × 10–12 |
| Farmer's carry (light, controlled, exhale) | 2 × 30 sec |
| Dead bug | 2 × 8/side |

**Progression:** Increase load by roughly 5–10% when all reps are completed at RPE 6–7. Avoid increasing load and volume in the same week.

---

## Week 12: Reassessment

- Repeat a submaximal step test or a 6-minute walk test (only if rehab approves) to compare fitness.
- Record resting HR, BP, and RPE at a fixed submaximal workload to show improvement without pushing to maximum.
- Review symptom log and any rehab feedback before setting the next block.

---

## Nutrition and Recovery Components

**Nutrition (general, refer to a dietitian for cardiac-specific plans):**
- Emphasise vegetables, fruit, wholegrains, legumes, oily fish, nuts, and olive oil.
- Limit sodium, saturated fat, and added sugar. Check labels on processed foods.
- Protein around 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day to support muscle maintenance. Spread across meals.
- Hydrate adequately. Confirm fluid restrictions with his cardiologist, if any.
- Avoid large heavy meals immediately before training.

**Recovery:**
- Aim for 7–8 hours of sleep. Poor sleep affects resting HR and BP.
- Keep stress management in the plan: walks, breathing practice, or mindfulness.
- Include at least one fully rest day per week.
- Advise him to avoid alcohol binges and to avoid stimulant supplements, including pre-workouts containing high caffeine or yohimbine.
- Smoking cessation, if relevant, is the single highest-impact change. Refer if needed.

**Medication note:** Ask him to take prescribed medications as directed and not to skip doses before training. Instruct him to carry GTN if prescribed and to know how to use it.

---

## Quick Reference: Session Checklist

- [ ] Resting HR and BP recorded (if requested)
- [ ] Symptom check at start
- [ ] Warm-up completed
- [ ] Strength work at RPE 6–7, no breath-holding
- [ ] Aerobic work at RPE 11–13, HR under ceiling
- [ ] Cool-down and recovery HR noted
- [ ] Symptoms logged, any concerns flagged to rehab team

---

**Final note:** This is a general template. Individualise it with his rehab team's parameters, his medication effects, and his feedback. Any change to intensity or new exercise should be discussed with the cardiac rehab team first.
